classification.head: sfla_svm
classification.architecture: ConvLSTM features + SFLA feature selection + SVM

transform.description: Original geometry: full-resolution non-local-means denoise, CLAHE, then resize; classifier sees the whole slice, never an ROI crop. Used for the untagged classifier checkpoint shipped with the repository.

warnings: The Kaggle brain-MRI classification dataset carries no patient identifiers, so samples can only be grouped by image identity (training groups byte-identical copies together). Scores from this dataset may still be optimistic if the same patient appears under unrelated filenames.

Using the dataset's own Training/Testing split. It is an IMAGE-level split: this dataset ships no patient identifiers, so slices from one patient may appear on both sides and the test score can be optimistic.
Dropped 134 Training images that are byte-identical to a Testing image, so the test score is not inflated by memorised copies. The Testing set itself was not modified.

Two classifier heads exist for this method: the ConvLSTM's softmax layer and an SVM on SFLA-selected ConvLSTM features. The sfla_svm head is served; the choice was made on validation macro-F1 (0.9893 SVM vs 0.9775 softmax) before the test set was opened.
The SVM's probabilities come from Platt scaling cross-fitted on the training split; they rank classes well but are not calibrated risk estimates.
Grad-CAM explains the ConvLSTM that produced the features, not the SVM's decision boundary.

segmentation_3d.split: volume-level held-out test (one volume per patient)
warnings: Volumes were brain-cropped and resampled to 128³ from 240×240×155, so the Dice below is measured at that resolution, not at the scanner's.
FLAIR only: the Decathlon volumes carry four co-registered sequences and this model reads one, which is the sequence whole-tumour extent is clearest in.
The decision threshold (0.80, not the default 0.5) was chosen on the validation volumes by sweeping 6 candidates. The test volumes took no part in that choice.

This volumetric model is not what the API serves. An upload is a single slice and a 3D U-Net needs the slices around it, so uploads are segmented by the 2D U-Net; this model's Dice is a volumetric result measured on held-out volumes.

Disclosure: these held-out volumes were segmented twice. First at the default decision threshold of 0.5 (test Dice 0.4406), before a threshold sweep on the *validation* volumes showed the model over-segmented by a factor of 2.5 and that 0.80 corrected it. The second pass, reported here, used that validation-chosen threshold. The choice never saw the test volumes, but the test set was read twice and saying so is part of the result.
